label: Double Double Whammy
description: Thx is Hannah Read's hushed, homespun early full-length as Lomelda, ten short songs of plainspoken lyrics over sparse acoustic and electric guitar, recorded with the DIY intimacy that defines her Silsbee, Texas project. It sits at the quiet, unresolved end of the 2010s Bandcamp folk scene, closer to a diary than a studio record.
lineage: An early document in the hemlock/Little Mazarn/Texas hushed-folk network Read has stayed close to; a direct precursor to the fuller-band M for Empathy and Hannah.

label: Double Double Whammy
description: M for Empathy is Hannah Read's most stripped-down Lomelda record, eleven brief, whispery songs built from silence, half-finished phrases and spare guitar. Read has described it as things said or unsaid finally let out, a record about making peace with her own voice.
lineage: The quietest turn in Lomelda's catalog between the full-band Thx and Hannah, deepening her ties to the Texas/hemlock hushed-folk network.

label: Double Double Whammy
description: Hannah is Read's most fleshed-out Lomelda album to date, fourteen tender, unhurried songs that move between fragile solo passages and warmer full-band arrangements while keeping her plainspoken, diaristic lyrics at the center. It is patient, intimate Texas indie folk built for close listening.
lineage: Widely regarded as Lomelda's breakthrough, consolidating the hushed songwriting of Thx and M for Empathy into a fuller sound shared with labelmates in the Double Double Whammy/hemlock orbit.

label: Captured Tracks
description: Plum is Widowspeak's warmest, most unhurried record, recorded with Sam Evian in the Catskills; Molly Hamilton's honeyed voice sits over dusty, sun-worn guitars and easy tempos that lean further into the band's country and 90s-dream-pop touchstones than the darker Expect the Best before it.
lineage: Follows Expect the Best and precedes The Jacket in Widowspeak's later-career turn toward a twangier, more overtly country-inflected version of their dream-pop sound.
borderline_note: Year corrected to 2020 (per the album's own Bandcamp page and Wikipedia); an earlier needs_verification note had left it unconfirmed.

label: Captured Tracks
description: Expect the Best is Widowspeak's heaviest, most nocturnal record, four-piece takes on somber indie rock, dream pop and what the band calls 'cowboy grunge.' Molly Hamilton's melodies stay pretty even as the songs sit in dread and self-doubt, recorded by Kevin McMahon (Swans, Real Estate).
lineage: Follows the duo-recorded All Yours and marks Widowspeak's shift to a full touring band, laying groundwork for the country-tinged twang that deepens on Plum and The Jacket.
borderline_note: Year corrected to 2017 (the album's own Bandcamp page and Wikipedia agree); an earlier needs_verification note guessed 2021.

label: Captured Tracks
description: The Jacket loosely tracks a fictional band's rise and fall through ten songs of layered guitars, dusty percussion and ambling bass; Widowspeak lean fully into their outlaw-country and slowcore reference points (Neil Young, Cowboy Junkies) while keeping Molly Hamilton's voice front and center.
lineage: The most explicitly twangy Widowspeak record to date, recorded back in New York with Homer Steinweiss and mixed by Chris Coady, extending the country turn begun on Plum.

label: Saddle Creek
description: Ada Lea's third album is her most playful and breezy, trading the moodier indie rock of her earlier records for '70s Laurel Canyon folk warmth, slice-of-life humor and knowing Dylan references in the song titles. Alexandra Levy's plainspoken voice carries loose, sun-drenched arrangements built for driving.
lineage: A late turn toward Cosmic American Music textures for a Montreal songwriter previously closer to art-rock; sits alongside Kate Bollinger and Courtney Marie Andrews' own Laurel Canyon-leaning records in this lane.
borderline_note: Ada Lea's earlier two albums are moodier indie rock without clear country/twang signifiers and are left out; only this Laurel Canyon-leaning record is included, per the ruling that pop/indie artists' country turns count as V/Core only where the album itself overlaps the sound.

album: I Keep My Feet on the Fragile Plane
label: Double Double Whammy
description: Allegra Krieger's Double Double Whammy debut is ten quietly contemplative songs, plainspoken and diaristic over patient fingerpicked guitar and occasional strings. It sits comfortably beside labelmates hemlock and Lomelda in its hushed, unhurried intimacy.
lineage: Part of the same Double Double Whammy roster as Lomelda and Told Slant, extending that label's hushed, confessional strand of indie folk.

label: Ruination Record Co.
description: Blue Ranger's first LP in five years bridges electronica, soft-folk and ambient rock, its rustic, anxious songs unfolding slowly around violin textures until they build to sudden, eureka-like releases. It is a patient record about processing memory in small, private moments.
lineage: A more collaborative, studio-focused turn for the band, growing out of the live-show chemistry Sammy Maine's liner notes describe.

label: Mtn Laurel Recording Co.
description: Eyes Like a Mirror is Carmen Perry's vivid, conversational solo debut away from Remember Sports, ten earthy, understated songs with a subtle twang running under her plainspoken delivery. It is a quieter, more intimate showcase for a songwriter used to power-pop punk.
lineage: A solo turn for Remember Sports' co-frontperson, moving from that band's power-pop toward the hushed, folk-leaning sound of labelmates on Mtn Laurel Recording Co. (also home to Sluice).

label: Self-released
description: Chuck Pond is the debut LP from Nashville's Charlie Hill (formerly recording as Chazzy Lake), a cleaner-toned set of indie country blending Laurel Canyon-inspired songwriting with ample pedal steel. Singles 'Dive In' and 'L.A. Fever' set the record's easy, open-road feel.
lineage: A friend and frequent tourmate of the Burlington, Vermont crew (Greg Freeman, Lily Seabird, Dari Bay), tying Nashville's indie-country scene to that network.

label: Earth Libraries
description: Eddy is the debut album from Chicago's Charlie Reed (a full band, not a solo artist), delicate and subdued folk-rock that swells into strings and pedal steel around themes of love, loss and cyclical anxiety. The band is known live for a striking Karen Dalton cover.
lineage: Part of the Earth Libraries roster's patient, string-laced strand of Midwest indie folk.

label: Keeled Scales
description: These Days is Emily Hines' efficient, lived-in folk-rock debut, seven songs built on sparse acoustic arrangements and a dynamic, expressive voice. It favors economy over ornamentation, letting small details carry the emotional weight.
lineage: Released on Keeled Scales, the Austin label that also carries Hataałii and other hushed Texas songwriters in this lane's orbit.

label: Loose Future
description: Valentine finds Courtney Marie Andrews leaning further into ornate, Laurel Canyon-styled folk, her Ronstadt-range voice wrapped in ethereal harmonies and a warm, '70s Nashville palette. It continues her run of self-released records on her own Loose Future imprint.
lineage: The latest chapter for a songwriter who moved from Fat Possum to her own label after Old Flowers and Loose Future, staying close to the Cosmic American Music revival this lane tracks.
borderline_note: Only one confirmed track title found within budget; add more key_tracks if a full tracklist source surfaces later.

album: A Swollen River, A Well Overflowing
label: Keeled Scales
description: Tenci's second album pairs Jess Shoman's raw, cracked-voiced folk songwriting with Curtis Oren's saxophone and guitar, a whimsical, homespun record that widens the intimate sound of their debut without losing its plainspoken core.
lineage: Follows My Heart Is an Open Field on the same Keeled Scales label, part of the Chicago DIY-folk scene that also includes Lomelda collaborators and Jessica Risker.
borderline_note: Only one confirmed additional track title found within budget.

label: Brutal Honest
description: Native State is Jess Williamson's early, spare full-length, plainspoken folk songs recorded with minimal backing that let her voice and guitar carry the weight. Its 'Seventh Song' became a favorite that critics kept returning to years later.
lineage: Predates the cosmic-country turn of Cosmic Wink and Sorceress, an early document of Williamson's move from Austin's DIY folk scene toward the wider Mexican Summer roster.
borderline_note: Only one confirmed key track; a fuller tracklist source was not reached within budget.

label: Paradise of Bachelors
description: Imitation of War is Kayla Cohen's fifth album as Itasca, patient, exploratory guitar-driven folk rock with feathery vocals that trade her earlier solo-guitar instrumentals for full, dreamlike band arrangements. It is unhurried, immersive music that rewards close listening.
lineage: Cohen's roots are in the American Primitive fingerstyle tradition of John Fahey and Jack Rose; this album folds that instrumental language into vocal-led indie folk on Paradise of Bachelors, the label behind Hiss Golden Messenger and William Tyler.
borderline_note: Only the title track confirmed as a key track within budget; secondary lane V8 reflects Cohen's American Primitive guitar background.
